names.name: βλίτον
names.note: Bland pot-herb without drug action; blite (Amaranthus blitum) standard.

names.name: Blites
names.note: White and red blites (Blitum) with beet-like leaves and tufted heads; usually referred to Amaranthus, species uncertain.

dsc:2.117.text: βλίτον λαχανεύεται καὶ τοῦτο. ἔστι δὲ εὐκοίλιον, οὐδεμίαν ἔχον φαρμακώδη δύναμιν.

cul:043-blites.text: They are all of them cooling, drying, and binding, serving to restrain the fluxes of blood in either man or woman, especially the red; which also stays the overflowing of the women’s reds, as the white Blites stays the whites in women. It is an excellent secret; you cannot well fail in the use. They are all under the dominion of Venus. There is another sort of wild Blites like the other wild kinds, but have long and spiky heads of greenish seeds, seeming by the thick setting together to be all seed. This sort the fishers are delighted with, and it is good and usual bait; for fishes will bite fast enough at them, if you have wit enough to catch them when they bite.
